first.rationale: Onboarding simplification directly addresses the current completion decline and has prior evidence of improving time-to-value and early adoption, making it the strongest current fit for sustainable revenue. Verify memory_86 for downstream quality and durability, and memory_73 to assess whether promotional pricing produced durable qualified revenue rather than acquisition lift driven by discounting. Until verified, favor a guarded onboarding test over a broad pricing response.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly matches the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle because its qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention -12% and failure through the first renewal cycle. The experiment remains preferable to a broad rollout because current activation weakness may not be entirely caused by onboarding.

final2.rationale: Continue with shortened onboarding despite the competitor’s deeper price cut. Verified evidence shows onboarding simplification improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is not justified: the verified 40% discount increased signups and near-term qualified revenue but reduced 30-day retention by 12%, with cohorts failing through first renewal. The doubled churn conversations increase urgency but do not overturn that known downstream harm. Use a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout because the present market shock may affect outcomes.
